To stop threads at the end of your Python script, you can use the `join()` method provided by the `threading` module. This method blocks the calling thread until the thread whose identity is given by the argument has terminated.

Here's how to do it:

```
import threading
import time

# Start a new thread
t = threading.Thread(target=my_function)
t.start()

# Do some other work...

# Wait for the thread to finish
t.join()
```

In your case, you can use this method after calling `thread.start()` and before your script ends. This will ensure that all threads have finished their execution before your script terminates.

Here's how you can modify your code:

```
for t in threads:
    t.join()  # Wait for each thread to finish
```

This way, you can be sure that all threads have terminated before your script ends.
